Inspection Reports
"The focus on pupils’ well-being promotes pupils to be happy and have a sense of self-worth. Pupils learn to understand their emotions and are well-supported." ISI Inspection Report, February 2024
We are delighted to share our Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection, which took place at Solefield 27th - 29th February 2024.
We are very proud to say that we met all standards, the highest grades possible under the new reporting framework, and the report is full of many positive and pleasing comments, as well as useful recommendations for the future. The full 2024 Inspection Report can be viewed here. Please also find below a selection of salient points:
Mental Health and Wellbeing
1. Leaders prioritise the mental health and emotional well-being of pupils. 2. The focus on pupils’ well-being promotes pupils to be happy and have a sense of self-worth. Pupils learn to understand their emotions and are well-supported. 3. Pupils gain a greater understanding of themselves and their individuality, as well as developing positive attitudes towards themselves and others. 4. Starting in the early years, leaders have effectively implemented a social emotional curriculum that teaches children how to self-regulate and understand their emotions. This continues throughout the school.
Academic
5. Pupils develop skills for lifelong learning. 6. Teachers demonstrate secure subject knowledge and effectively cultivate a positive and inclusive classroom environment. 7. Pupils acquire knowledge and make progress, unafraid of making mistakes. 8. Pupils are articulate communicators and speak confidently, expressing their views clearly. 9. They develop collaborative skills and independence. 10. Pupils are well-prepared for the next stage of education, including moving to their senior school. 11. Older pupils speak confidently in different contexts, have well-developed literacy skills, and effectively employ a variety of linguistic techniques in their writing.
Behaviour
12. Pupils behave well and understand the effect their actions may have on others. 13. Staff expect older pupils to set a good example for others and they fulfil this expectation. 14. Pupils demonstrate politeness and thoughtfulness and confidently engage with adults. 15. Pupils demonstrate an understanding of right and wrong and recognise the importance of adhering to rules and guidelines, contributing to a positive and respectful school environment where pupils feel safe and valued. 16. Kindness is seen as important. 17. Pupils’ behaviour aligns with the school's core values of valuing oneself and others.
Extra-curricular
18. There is a wide-ranging extra-curricular programme which is valued by both pupils and parents. 19. The wide range of team and individual sports offered enables pupils to find a sporting activity that suits them. 20. Pupils developed their personal health and physical education through an effective physical education and games program delivered by specialist staff. Relationships with staff 21. Pupils feel well-supported by adults who know them personally and actively encourage their participation in school activities. 22. Supportive relationships between class teachers and pupils are nurtured from a young age. 23. Teachers build strong connections with pupils throughout the school. 24. Leaders... place much emphasis on mutual respect and the individuality of all pupils. 25. School ethos of inclusion for all.
Pupil voice
26. Pupils... feel that their voices are both heard and valued. 27. A collaborative and inclusive school environment where pupil voices are heard and respected. 28. The importance of inclusivity and upholding British values are recognised throughout the school. 29. The active Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Committee organise events to raise awareness of diversity, which promote mutual respect and celebrate the individuality of all people.
Community
30. Pupils are actively engaged in activities that foster their understanding of the world beyond the school, reflecting their aim to value the world. 31. Through initiatives led by the charity committee, pupils participate and are successful in fundraising for both regional and national charities. 32. School leaders facilitate meaningful interactions with the local community.
Whilst it is wonderful to receive so much positive feedback, we are, as always, reflective of what we as a school could do better. We strive to ensure that pupil focus remains consistent at all times; the three recommendations given by ISI are ones which we are enacting upon, and which will help us to become a better school.

Drama
“I loved saying all my lines and making people laugh.” Louis, Year 2
The main purpose of Drama at Solefield is to develop self-confidence, trust, working collaboratively and empathy, we understand that through creativity we can foster these skills. No matter what a pupil’s ability may be, their contributions are respected and appreciated.
The children love acting and thrive in drama lessons which are planned to develop character and self-belief. Timetabled lessons introduce pupils to improvisation, speaking in public, script writing and empathy. Learning to work as a team member is an essential skill which is developed.
As well as regular drama lessons, all our pupils participate in several performances every year to their parents, peers, staff and governors. This begins in the first few weeks for children joining us in Reception, who perform in our Harvest Festival celebration. Drama is further promoted with educational visits to London theatres and Shakespeare’s Globe.
Each pupil performs in an annual year group performance, ranging from nativity plays in the Pre-Prep to the Shakespeare Schools’ Festival in Year 7, performing such classics as Henry V, The Tempest and Macbeth. Pupils who stay with us until Year 8 perform in a gala for parents and staff and is a real highlight and fitting tribute to their time at Solefield.
There are a wide range of other performances throughout the year too, both individual and ensemble. Pupils with a particular love of drama in Years 7 and 8 are nurtured in this through our specialist Drama Scholarship Pathway, in which they devote one afternoon per week to studying and enjoying this with our Head of Drama.
Years 6 and 7 pupils have recently performed the Lion King, Bugsy Malone, The Pirate Pretender, Guys & Dolls, The Rocky Monster Show, Joseph and the Technicolour Dreamcoat and Henry VIII the Tudor Dude.

Headmistress' Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to Solefield School, where we nurture a genuine love of learning alongside kindness, integrity and resilience.
At Solefield, small class sizes, typically 12–14 pupils, ensure every child is truly known, supported and encouraged to thrive. While we are proud of our strong academic outcomes, our focus is firmly on educating the whole child. Wellbeing sits at the heart of school life, supported by a close partnership with parents and our nurturing school environment.
Our values, Value yourself. Value others. Value our world, underpin everything we do. They are lived daily by our pupils and staff, and even our beloved wellbeing dogs, Monty and Charlie, play their part in creating a warm and supportive atmosphere.
Our Lower School continues to grow in strength and popularity, with increasing demand and waiting lists in the younger year groups. From September 2026, we are proud to expand to two-form entry in Reception for the first time, an exciting milestone that reflects the quality of our provision. Over the following two years, we plan to extend this model through to Year 6 as part of our transition to full co-education. As we continue to grow and develop, Solefield Local Governors have taken the strategic decision to focus on educating children from Little Acorns through to Year 6. Our final Year 7 cohort will join us in September 2026.
This strategic shift enables us to further strengthen our Upper Prep offering, including the development of a distinctive Year 6 “Thinking Curriculum”. This exciting programme may include opportunities such as Chess, Forest School, Debating, Critical Thinking, Philosophy, Latin and Pottery, encouraging curiosity, creativity and intellectual independence.
At Solefield, we aim to develop kind, thoughtful and resilient young people, equipped not only for academic success but for life beyond the classroom.
I would be delighted to meet with you. Please visit us at one of our Open Mornings or contact our Registrar, Mrs Savage to arrange a visit on 01732 452 142, email [email protected].
Helen McClure Headmistress

Music
“I love playing the violin with my class and it is really fun.” Benedict, Year 3
Our all-inclusive policy extends to Music, in which all pupils are introduced to the fundamental activities of performing, listening and composing. Solefield has a purpose-built music school which helps to foster a strong tradition of playing and performing. This is reflected in the large percentage of pupils who have individual music lessons on a wide variety of instruments.
Reception children experience rhythm, percussion and singing. Pupils in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 learn the recorder, Years 3 the violin, Year 4 the melodica, and Year 5 the ukulele. Pupils in Years 6, 7 and 8 have keyboard lessons in our custom-built keyboard room.
All pupils perform in year group concerts where emphasis is on participation and enjoyment. In addition, there are informal concerts throughout the year as well as more formal events. The school has three choirs, two orchestras, as well as string, woodwind, cello, guitar and brass groups. Many of the children participate in a rock/technology group learning performance and recording techniques. Pupils regularly gain scholarships to senior school.

Wrap Around Care
We are pleased to work with parents and offer wraparound care (Breakfast Club and After School Care) and a Solefield dedicated Transport Service. We also run an extensive range of clubs before and after school and parents may use this option or a mixture of both.
How to book Breakfast Club, After School Care and Transport Service:
Via SOCS, our online booking system here.
Breakfast Club – 7.30-8.00am
We operate a Breakfast Club between 7:30am and 8:00am. The cost is £6 per session, with breakfast options provided for children.
After School Care – 4.00-6.00pm (6.30pm by arrangement)
After School Care (including tea) runs from 4:00pm until 6.00pm, (with a 6.30pm pick-up option available).
There are four timings options available:
An additional charge of £25 per half hour will be made for any pupils not picked up by 6.00pm (or 6.30pm if booking is made in advance).
Depending on the day and the children staying, there may be activities organised in After School Care. There will always be the opportunity for children to read, work quietly and play.
The After School Care Mobile (between 4-6.30pm) is: 07857 851746.
Wait Class is available for all Pre-Prep children (Little Acorns to Year 2) with older siblings or for those staying for After School Care and ends at 4pm. Should you wish your child to attend Wait Class, please sign them up using our online booking system, SOCS here.

Yr 3-6 Curriculum (KS2)
“Pupils’ attitudes to learning are outstanding.” ISI Inspection Report 2019
At Solefield, we provide a modern and dynamic classroom environment, whilst maintaining and encouraging the traditional values of learning one would expect of a highly successful and well-established Prep School.
As well as traditional subjects, all pupils study French, Music, Art and Drama from Reception upwards. Alongside this, there is ample opportunity to augment their learning and develop their creativity using a variety of resources from programming Beebots to re-enacting Greek myths in Latin.
We have an excellent staff of subject specialists who deliver exciting and clearly differentiated lessons. To enrich our teaching further, we have enhanced digital delivery of lessons and introduced iPads. Pupils enjoy Pupil Progress Interviews, individualised differentiation and an improved programme of self and peer assessment.
Outstanding classroom practice is central to our success, along with fostering an all-encompassing love of learning. Small class sizes enable staff to individualise the learning programme for each pupil whilst taking the time and effort to get to know them, personally and academically. We encourage assiduous and frequent questioning and we instil the resolution to improve. These, and our enrichment of the academic curriculum, produce happy, inquisitive children with the confidence to learn successfully.
It is our aim to exercise and stretch all of our pupils’ minds so they acquire a passion for learning. We also strive to ensure that the pupil is given the ability and motivation to take ownership of their own learning through developing independence and giving a strong sense of self-esteem and an inquiring mind. Our intention is for students to become life-long learners and develop the necessary transferable skills that will equip them for the fast-changing life beyond Solefield.

Art

Art is taught by subject specialists throughout the school from our Little Acorns and Reception to Year 8. The purpose-built Art room offers a wide range of activities, including painting, sculpture, ceramics and printing. Our art curriculum is designed to foster creativity, nurture the pupils’ imaginations and encourage self-expression.

A highlight of the year is our whole school Art Exhibition, where every child in the school displays some of their work to be admired.
Art at Solefield is fun, but we also have very high standards and this is reflected in the large number of art scholarships gained in recent years. Learning is further enhanced by visiting artists, gallery trips and the art clubs on offer.

pageCache.text:
Step into Solefield

Sustainability at Solefield
“I feel really proud that I am making a difference in helping to make our school greener.” Gabriel, Year 8 Eco Prefect
One of our school values is to ‘value our world’.
We are committed to nurturing a generation of environmentally aware, responsible, and proactive young people. Sustainability is woven through every aspect of school life - from our curriculum and daily routines to how we care for our surroundings and engage with our community.
A Whole-School Commitment
Sustainability is not a single initiative; it is a shared responsibility across the entire school. We take a coordinated, long-term approach that includes teaching and learning, site management, and community engagement.
Learning for the Future
We embed environmental awareness across the curriculum, ensuring pupils understand the challenges facing our planet and feel empowered to make a difference.
By the time they leave Solefield, pupils are informed, thoughtful, and ready to play their part in a changing world.
Sustainability is explored across all subjects
Reducing Our Environmental Impact
We are actively working to reduce our environmental footprint through practical and measurable steps.
Our goal is steady, meaningful progress that makes a real difference.
Improving energy efficiency across the school
Encouraging energy-conscious behaviour
Auditing and reducing carbon use over time
Waste and Responsible Use
We promote a culture of reducing waste and using resources wisely.
Working to minimise food waste
Nature, Grounds and Biodiversity
Our school environment is a living classroom. We are enhancing biodiversity and creating spaces where pupils can connect with nature.
Tree planting and wildflower areas
Outdoor learning opportunities
Habitat creation and conservation
Sustainable Travel and Community
We work with families and the wider community to encourage more sustainable choices.
Walking, cycling, and car-sharing initiatives
School events and awareness campaigns
Engaging parents in sustainability efforts
Pupil Voice and Leadership
Pupils play an active role in shaping our sustainability journey.
Eco Council initiatives and campaigns
Opportunities to lead projects and share ideas
Regular feedback helping to guide school priorities
Looking Ahead
Our Sustainability and Climate Action Plan sets out clear priorities, actions, and measurable goals for the future. We regularly review our progress and continue to build on what we achieve.
Our Approach
Everything we do is guided by a few simple principles:
Practical – focusing on achievable actions
Integrated – part of everyday school life
Progressive – improving over time
Inclusive – involving the whole community

Mathematics
Mathematics at Solefield is a serious but enjoyable affair. It not only permeates other curriculum subjects, such as STEM, Science, Geography and Physical Education, it is also integral to our students’ lives. That is one of the key tenets of learning Mathematics: it is an essential, relevant life skill and Solefield pupils understand that.
The Mathematics curriculum at Solefield has a flow to it, from Pre-Prep all the way up to Year 8. The students’ mathematical journey is well-planned, well-delivered and tailored to each pupil’s needs. While we are mindful of the fact that our students do take important exams during their time at school, especially in Years 6-8, that is not the main driving force behind our vision. We aspire to produce competent, confident mathematicians with a love of learning who are well-equipped to problem solve. Teachers and Teaching Assistants support and encourage all learners; consolidating the basics and stretching those who thrive on the challenge.
As such, pupils are given the responsibility of selecting work that they feel provides them with the level of stretch they need during each lesson. Sometimes they require a helping hand in choosing which work to attempt, but that is all part of the learning process.
Pre-Prep provides the cornerstone of Mathematics at Solefield, covering the basic number concepts using a cyclical curriculum. Regular review of topics enables learners to keep their mathematical skills sharp and build on prior learning in a sequential manner. Practical activities play a huge role in ensuring concepts are embedded using the ‘concrete, pictorial, abstract’ approach to learning. Group work and discussion also provide opportunities for pupils to deepen their understanding and develop their collaboration skills.
However, the Pre-Prep also prepares them for their Maths lessons in Year 3 and beyond. They start to record their work carefully and methodically from Year 1, learning the importance of presenting their working out in a logical manner.
Years 3 and 4 build on all of the hard work already put in during lessons in the Pre-Prep. The biggest focus during these years are times tables - the foundation of much of their future learning. Through the use of interactive games and websites such as Times Tables Rock Stars, students learn these in an engaging manner. By the end of Year 4, times tables should be recalled forwards, backwards and inside out! It is during these years that we enter the First Mathematical Challenge in which our pupils score highly, some achieving a treasured Full Marks certificate.
During the key Years of 5 and 6, students work at pace, with accuracy and a focus on their presentation. The curriculum becomes increasingly complex, with more abstract concepts introduced. Their work involves mastery of topics as we aim to work above the National Curriculum expectation for their age. Skills are put to good use in the Primary Mathematics Challenge, that all pupils enter. We have great success in this with many students progressing onto the Bonus Round.
For those pupils who elect to stay on for Years 7 and 8, the learning becomes even more individualised to suit their needs. We follow the Common Entrance syllabus, which prepares them well for the GCSE curriculum. As our pupils’ behaviour for learning continues to mature, so does the level of responsibility we give them in guiding their own mathematical journey. Fortunately, at Solefield we have the expertise within the department to really challenge and push those for whom Mathematics is a passion and a talent. We also enter our Seniors into the Junior Mathematics Challenge and subsequent Junior Kangaroo.
Our vision at Solefield is to produce confident and competent mathematicians who can solve real-life problems. This guides what we teach and when we teach it, from the first day a pupil starts at school until their final lesson. Not only does this mean they develop a love of learning, and a love of learning Maths, it also enables them to perform well in the exams they take. Children leave Solefield ready to tackle the mathematical world around them, the one they currently inhabit and the one they will encounter during the rest of their lives.
Our commitment to this vision, to supporting our pupils in becoming confident in solving real-world problems, was acknowledged when we became an NRICH Problem-Solving School in February 2024. This award was pleasing recognition for the time, effort and focus we place on developing these skills in our Mathematics curriculum and across many aspects of Solefield in general.
Mr Budden Assistant Head, Head of Mathematics & Director of STEM
